criterion: Every surface of the home page, the pricing page and the timeline editor keeps to black, white and grey, with a green to amber to orange gradient as the one chromatic colour.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when those pages use neutrals everywhere apart from the green, amber and orange gradient. Answer no when any other hue fills a surface, colours text or marks a status, or when a page is washed in one hue.

criterion: On the projects table and the versions table, status reads as words on neutral chips, a red appears only beside failure or deletion, and secondary text steps down by opacity of the same ink.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the brand gradient appears only as a gradient accent, success shows a word with a tick on a neutral chip, red is kept for failures and destructive actions, and text hierarchy comes from lighter or darker ink. Answer no when the gradient becomes a flat fill, text colour or status colour, or when red or extra hues mark ordinary states.

criterion: The glowing outline around the Pro card on the pricing page carries colour along roughly two fifths of its edge and plain white along the rest.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the Pro card outline is lopsided, with the gradient concentrated on one stretch and white elsewhere. Answer no when the colours run evenly round the whole edge or the card has a plain border.

criterion: Raised surfaces in the timeline editor sit at distinguishable elevation levels, and tracks, items and the selected item separate by elevation in place of drawn borders.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when panels, tracks, items and the selection read as stacked levels of lightening surface. Answer no when the editor relies on outlines to separate them or when the levels look identical.

criterion: The application routes such as the dashboard and the timeline editor are designed dark, and the home page alternates designed dark bands with designed light bands.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the signed-in routes are dark throughout and the home bands switch between finished dark and light grounds. Answer no when the application is light or the home page sits on a single ground.

criterion: Type across the home page and the timeline editor uses one grotesque family in two widths, the wider width only on the home hero line, with monospace confined to the code editor and to columns of aligned figures.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when headings and body share one sans family, the hero line is set wider, and timecodes, amounts and counts line up in columns. Answer yes only if monospace shows up solely in the code editor or beside aligned numbers; answer no when several families mix or figures jitter in stacked columns.

criterion: Reading pages such as the blog index and the privacy page grow with the browser's text size, and the timeline editor chrome keeps its size until the interface scale setting changes.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when enlarging browser text enlarges blog and privacy copy while the editor furniture stays put, and the settings scale enlarges the editor. Answer no when reading pages stay fixed or the editor reflows with browser text.

criterion: Display headings on the home page and the pricing page scale with the window width, and cards round most, fields and buttons round less, and pill controls take a full pill shape.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when display type grows and shrinks with the window and the corner family shows three distinct softness levels. Answer no when headings jump between fixed sizes or every element shares one corner.

criterion: The home page opens on the live product with generous space around each band, and the timeline editor reads as a dense operational tool with stage, timeline and parameter panel together.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the home page leads with the drawn product and breathes, and the editor fits its three regions on a laptop screen as a quiet working tool. Answer no when the home page leads with generic marketing or the editor scatters its regions across scrolling pages.

criterion: Elements on the home page rise into place with the fade completing early, headings arrive line by line from each line's own height, the home statement arrives word by word, and horizontal rules draw themselves open.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when scrolling the home page shows those entrance behaviours. Answer no when content pops in, slides as whole blocks, or rules appear already drawn with motion enabled.

criterion: Movement across the home page and the timeline editor leaves quickly and settles slowly on one shared set of curves, the customer wall is the only looping movement, the dial knob is the only overshoot, and every revealing element behaves alike.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when motion feels consistent everywhere with a single loop on the customer wall and a single overshoot on the dial. Answer no when components move at unrelated speeds, several elements loop on their own, or several elements bounce.

criterion: With a reduced-motion preference, every reveal on the home page appears at once and the keychain hero holds a still frame.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the reduced-motion setting shows every home band in its end state and a still keychain. Answer no when reveals still animate or the scene keeps moving under that setting.

criterion: Controls on the pricing page, the consent panel and the timeline editor show resting, pointed-at, pressed, focused and unavailable states, unavailable controls carry more than a colour change, and hover styling applies only on hovering pointers.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each of those states is visible and an unavailable control also changes shape, icon or wording. Answer no when a state is missing, unavailable is colour alone, or a tapped control stays in its hover look on touch.

criterion: Text on the home page, the pricing page and the timeline editor meets WCAG 2.2 AA, with body text at 4.5:1 and large text and components at 3:1 against their grounds, touch targets at the WCAG 2.2 minimum target size, and flashing held to three times a second at most.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when measured contrast and target sizes meet those bars on the three surfaces and nothing flashes faster. Answer no when faint text, small targets or rapid flashing appear.

criterion: Form controls on the login and signup routes keep persistent visible labels in single centred forms, icon-only controls in the timeline editor carry text labels, the dial in the parameter panel announces its value, and the home keychain scene is hidden from assistive technology with the heading beside the scene carrying its meaning.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when every field shows a label above or beside it, icon buttons have accessible names, a screen reader hears the dial value, and the hero scene is skipped by assistive technology. Answer no when placeholders stand in for labels, icon buttons are unnamed, or the scene is announced as content.

criterion: The focus indicator on the home page and the pricing page sits offset from each control edge for keyboard focus alone, focusing an unrevealed element reveals the element at once, and the consent panel announces itself on arrival.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when keyboard focus draws an offset ring that pointer clicks do not, hidden content appears when focused, and assistive technology announces the consent panel. Answer no when any of those behaviours is missing.

criterion: At tablet width the pricing cards drop to two across, on a wide screen four purchasable cards sit above the Enterprise card, and at every width the home page and pricing page scroll sideways only inside the marquees and the comparison table's own area.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the pricing grid rearranges at those widths and the page body never scrolls sideways. Answer no when cards overflow, stay four across on a tablet, or the whole page scrolls horizontally.

criterion: The keychain hero on the home page is drawn live in the browser from separate pieces, a chain of one repeated link with distinct charms, and the chain, clasp and key read as polished metal.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the hero shows a lit, reflective keychain assembled from repeated links, a clasp, a key and several different charms. Answer yes only if the browser draws the scene itself; answer no when the hero is a flat picture, a video, or a single dull shape.

criterion: The keychain hero on the home page shows a still of the same composition during loading, and the heading and Get Started action are readable before the live scene arrives.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a slow load shows the heading, the action and a matching still in place of an empty box. Answer no when the heading waits for the scene or a blank area appears.

criterion: On the pricing page the plan cards and the comparison table show the same prices and limits, each paid card lists only its own additions after its everything-in line, the table keeps row labels and plan names in view and names missing rows in words, and Enterprise topics lead to a sales conversation.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when every figure matches between cards and table, card lists are cumulative, the table headings stay visible while scrolling with not-included written out, and Enterprise offers Contact Sales only. Answer no when any figure disagrees, cards repeat earlier plans' lines, or Enterprise features look purchasable.

criterion: Blocks drawn by member code in the timeline editor run apart from the page, playback continues during block rendering, code errors appear beneath the code editor with the stage intact, and a block can be placed on a track from the keyboard.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a code block cannot touch the page or session, the editor keeps playing while blocks render, an error shows under the code editor, and keyboard placement works. Answer no when code affects the page, playback stalls, an error breaks the stage, or placement needs a mouse.

criterion: Lists such as the projects table, the review inbox and the brand kits page show an empty state naming the action that fills them, loading content arrives as skeletons shaped like the content, and a failed panel offers a retry with the rest of the route working.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when those empty, loading and failure states appear as described. Answer no when a list is blank with a lone spinner, the layout collapses while loading, or one failure takes down the whole route.

criterion: The brand kits page shows colour swatches with font names, the favourites page reuses the library cards, the blog index lists posts as dated rows with category chips, and the not-found page keeps the header and footer.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all four surfaces look as described. Answer no when any of them drops those elements or invents a different card style.

criterion: One shared token set styles the home page and the timeline editor alike, each view leads with one main action, and the home bands show the product drawing itself, with a drawn timeline diagram wherever footage is absent.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when colours, corners and type match between marketing and editor, each view has one dominant action, and home pictures are drawn by the product. Answer no when the two surfaces look like different products, views compete with several main actions, or the home page relies on screenshots.

criterion: The product route expands the four pillars, import, edit, enhance and ship, into full bands, and the privacy page states how long each kind of record is kept.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each pillar has its own band on the product route and the privacy page lists a keeping period per kind of record. Answer no when the pillars are a single list or retention periods are missing.

criterion: The block library name filter settles once typing pauses, the block library stays smooth with several thousand blocks, and the marketing routes load only the two type widths the product uses.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when filtering waits for a pause, a long library scrolls smoothly, and only two font widths are fetched. Answer no when the filter jumps on every keystroke, the list stutters, or extra widths load.

criterion: The pricing page or the timeline editor offers an organisation console, single sign-on, a card checkout, a stock media library, captioning, speech synthesis, background removal, template saving, server-rendered frames, viewer watermarks, a site search, a second language or an offline mode.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when any of those features is offered anywhere in the product. Answer no when the product carries none of them, and the coming soon rows on the pricing page stay unperformed.
